question: A Claude-drafted notice about a service change is going out to every customer tomorrow. Which sequence of steps is correct?
options: A) Have the accountable owner review it; publish the notice to customers; check the facts against the source; obtain the required sign-off.
B) Check the facts against the source; have the accountable owner review it; obtain the required sign-off; publish the notice to customers.
C) Publish the notice to customers; check the facts against the source; have the accountable owner review it; obtain the required sign-off.
D) Obtain the required sign-off; check the facts against the source; publish the notice to customers; have the accountable owner review it.
correct_answers: B) Check the facts against the source; have the accountable owner review it; obtain the required sign-off; publish the notice to customers.
explanations: Incorrect. The owner reviews unverified content, and the notice is published before either the fact check or the sign-off has happened.
Correct. Factual checking comes first because the owner's judgment depends on accurate content, sign-off follows a completed review, and publication is the last irreversible step.
Incorrect. Publication comes before every check, which means any error reaches customers before anyone has looked for it.
Incorrect. Sign-off is given before anything has been checked, and the owner's review lands after customers have already received the notice.
